competing_explanation: Batch age is a confounder: hotter-stored batches were also older (9 vs 4 months), so age-driven degradation could fully explain the observed potency loss rather than temperature.
hypothesis_statement: VERDICT: FALSE, because the only evidence for C3 (record D2) is a confounded observational correlation that fails to control for batch age, so it cannot support the causal claim that higher storage temperature causes potency loss.
predicted_outcome: If temperature were truly the cause, an age-matched or randomized comparison holding batch age constant would still show a significant temperature-potency effect.
refutation_criterion: An age-matched analysis showing no significant association between storage temperature and potency loss once batch age is controlled would falsify the causal claim.
